question: Should the agent activity timeline be built as a UI/CLI projection over the metadata-audit and subagent-lifecycle contracts, or should this issue remain a separate first-class timeline feature with its own storage/API shape?
rationale: The current code has several plausible building blocks, but choosing the storage owner, Gateway/CLI contract, retention, redaction, and UI placement is product/security intent rather than a safe cleanup decision.

options.title: Build on audit and lifecycle contracts
options.body: Implement the timeline after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98521 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/38626 define the durable metadata and lifecycle receipt model.

options.title: Scope a standalone timeline
options.body: Approve a separate first-class timeline contract now, accepting the extra design work to avoid duplicating existing Activity, trajectory, task, and audit semantics.

options.title: Keep only existing observability
options.body: Decline a dedicated timeline for now and rely on Activity, sessions tail/export-trajectory, tasks, and diagnostics for operator inspection.

recommendation.title: Build on audit and lifecycle contracts
recommendation.body: Implement the timeline after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98521 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/38626 define the durable metadata and lifecycle receipt model.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the related metadata-audit direction and has recent current-main history in the adjacent Activity/docs and trajectory surfaces.
